untested: Whether coastal sea-salt deposition raises soil sodium and weakens aggregates. No paper matched this wording.

web.text: Coastal soils do show more exchangeable sodium close to the coast, with soils nearest the shore past saline-sodic limits and 1.5-2 km inland not. One Egyptian transect showed no steady trend. No source measured aggregate stability, so the aggregate-weakening step is untested.

untested: Whether soil Streptomyces aerosols seed cloud droplets or ice. Four papers matched but all are unrelated (enzyme expression, indoor spore release).

web.text: Raindrops are known to throw soil bacteria into the air, and fungal spores can act as ice nuclei. Nothing found on Streptomyces or geosmin particles acting as cloud nuclei.

untested: Phage killing of methane-oxidizing bacteria and its effect on methane oxidation.

papers.title: T4-type phages diversity in wetland soils reveals their ubiquity and their likely host-dependent dynamics

web.text: No soil study shows phage lysis lowering methane uptake. A bioreactor report says phage blooms can set back methane oxidizers, supporting the direction. A lake study found phages that carry a methane-oxidation gene, which hints at the opposite effect. Sediment work found viruses infect methanotrophs but their genes do not directly drive methane metabolism.

untested: Soil respiration response to aerosol-scattered light. The matched paper models carbon fluxes in smoke haze.

papers.title: Modeling the radiative effects of biomass burning aerosols on carbon fluxes in the Amazon region

web.text: Smoke haze with moderate aerosol raised canopy photosynthesis, which supports the first step. Nobody has measured the root or soil respiration response. A 2025 preprint calls the root-respiration link largely theoretical. Near volcanoes, geological CO2 can be mistaken for soil respiration.

papers.title: Litter microbial and soil faunal communities stimulated in the wake of a volcanic eruption in a semi‐arid woodland in Patagonia, Argentina
Influence of volcanic ash on infectivity and reproduction of two species of meloidogyne

web.text: After the 2011 Puyehue-Cordon Caulle ash fall in Patagonia, nematode numbers and soil enzyme activity dropped. That study did not report life-history (c-p) groups, so the claim about which nematodes go first is untested.

untested: Whether protist and earthworm silicon pools lower catchment silica export.

papers.title: Phytolith transport in soil: a laboratory study on intact soil cores
The ultrastructure of Heleopera petricola an agglutinate soil amoeba; with comments on feeding and silica deposition

web.text: Silica-shelled soil amoebae make a silicon pool about half the size of tree uptake in a beech forest, and stream silica exports were too high for rock weathering alone. That suggests biological pools feed silica exports, possibly the opposite of this prediction. Nothing found on earthworms.

untested: Whether real lightning strikes raise gene transfer in the field. The lab step is shown.

papers.title: Isolation of lightning-competent soil bacteria

web.text: Lab-scale lightning moved genes into bacteria in soil, and lightning-competent soil bacteria were isolated. One estimate puts the affected soil at 2 to 950 cubic metres per strike. Natural field transfer has not been shown, and no study looked at microbes in fulgurites or strike zones.
